item.title: 34th Annual Women in Leadership Conference
item.description:
34th Annual Women in Leadership Conference

PURCHASE YOUR TICKETS HERE

Michigan Business Women at Ross presents the 34th Annual Women in Leadership Conference (WiLC)!

​Join us for the 2026 WiLC at Michigan Ross on Friday, October 9, 2026, for a day of bold ideas, candid conversations, and meaningful connection.

​This year’s theme, Answer the Call, challenges us to move beyond the traditional leadership playbook and create space for the conversations that shape women’s lives and careers. From career and family to financial independence, appearance bias, relationship status, and coalition building across identities and backgrounds, WiLC will explore what it truly means to define leadership on your own terms.

​Through dynamic speakers and conversations spanning finance, beauty, fashion, sports, media, and beyond, you’ll hear from women who are challenging expectations, shaping industries, and creating new paths forward.

​Come to be inspired. Stay for the conversations. Leave ready to answer your call.

From Friday, October 9, 2026 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM EDT at Blau Colloquium.

item.title: ISBA Education Session #4: Recruiting Prep: Interviews, Behaviorals, & Casing Across Different Paths
item.description:
ISBA Education Session #4: Recruiting Prep: Interviews, Behaviorals, & Casing Across Different Paths

ISBA Education Session #4: Recruiting Prep: Interviews, Behaviorals, & Casing Across Different Paths
October 9 | 4 PM | R2220

Interview prep looks different depending on what you’re recruiting for. Technical rounds, casing, behaviorals, each require different preparation. So what should you actually be working on for your path?

In our 4th ISBA Education series, we’ll break down preparation across finance, consulting, marketing, product and GM roles, including technical and quantitative questions, case interviews, online assessments, take-home assignments, and behaviorals. We’ll discuss what each format asks of you, how to structure your answers, and how to make practice useful. You’ll hear from MBA2s about how they prepared for their specific roles, which resources helped, how they practiced with others, and what they wish they’d started earlier.

Panel:
1. Akshat Kishore: Summer Associate - Strategy & Product, Emergence Software Technologies, Inc. (Financial Services)
2. ⁠Anmol Chaudhri: MBA Summer Intern, OC&C Strategy Consultants (Consulting)
3. ⁠Kavin Senthil: Brand Marketing Intern, Danone North America (Consumer Packaged Goods)
4. ⁠Srinath Kausheeka: Technical Product Manager Intern, eBay Inc. (Technology)

Come with your questions and leave with a clearer sense of what to prioritize in Fall for your own recruiting path.

From Friday, October 9, 2026 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM EDT at R2220.

item.title: Rebuilding Democracy Osita Nwanevu in conversation with Elizabeth Anderson on the American Crossroads
item.description:
Rebuilding Democracy Osita Nwanevu in conversation with Elizabeth Anderson on the American Crossroads

Full description here: Rebuilding Democracy | Happening @ Michigan

 

As the country heads into the 2026 midterm elections, the University of Michigan welcomes journalist Osita Nwanevu, contributing editor at The New Republic and columnist at The Guardian, for a public conversation with Elizabeth Anderson, the John Dewey Distinguished University Professor of Philosophy.

The evening centers on Nwanevu's new book, The Right of the People: Democracy and the Case for a New American Founding, which argues that America's democratic troubles run deeper than any single election. The real problem, Nwanevu contends, lies in institutions that were never designed to let majorities govern, and in an economy that keeps power far from ordinary people.

Anderson, one of the country's most influential political philosophers, brings her own work on democracy, equality, and the workplace to the exchange. Together they take up the questions this election season keeps surfacing. Who really holds power in America? Why do so many people feel unheard, and what would it take to build a democracy worthy of the name?

The conversation is free and open to students, faculty, and the broader Ann Arbor community, with time for audience questions.

Schedule

Friday, October 9, 2026 at Ross School of Business, Robertson Auditorium

5:30 pm Doors open, light refreshments and Literati book sales in the lobby.
6:00 pm The program begins, including questions and answers at the end.
7:30 pm Refreshments and book signing / sales in the lobby until 8:00 pm.



From Friday, October 9, 2026 5:30 PM to 8:00 PM EDT at Ross School of Business - Robertson Auditorium.

item.title: SAS Public Open House
item.description:
SAS Public Open House

Open houses are free, inclusive opportunities to learn about astronomy and experience the universe firsthand. At each open house, members of SAS operate the telescopes and the planetarium of the Angell Hall Observatory. Guests can view astronomical objects through the 8-inch telescopes and the 0.4m telescope (weather permitting), watch a planetarium show on a number of interesting topics, or learn about the cosmos from a presentation. No special registrations or reservations are required, these events are entirely free to students and members of the public alike. 

The Angell Hall Observatory is located on the roof of Angell Hall. Take the elevator to the 5th floor to find the door to the roof down the hall.

The Angell Hall Planetarium is located on the third floor of Angell Hall, in room 3118.

From Friday, October 9, 2026 9:00 PM to 11:00 PM EDT at Angell Hall.

item.title: Gettin' in the Groove: An All-Levels Solo Jazz Series
item.description:
Gettin' in the Groove: An All-Levels Solo Jazz Series
Register here! 
 
Explore solo jazz dancing in this four week series with Sarah Beth! 

Each week students will learn a new set of classic jazz steps, a short sequence to solidify their learning, and engage in solo social dancing. Regardless of your swing dancing experience level, there will be something new for everyone! 

No solo jazz experience required. Attendees who have experience in solo jazz will have the opportunity to try new variations and explore new concepts with their dancing. 
Classes are progressive but since this series is not partnered, students may miss classes and rejoin later in the series.
 

When:
Sundays 7-9pm, Sept 13, 20 Oct 11, 18
Classes are progressive but since this series is not partnered, students may miss classes and rejoin later in the series.


Where:
Hoover St Studio, 323 E Hoover Ave, Ann Arbor MI


Instructor Bio:
Sarah Beth (SB) is a dancer, teacher, choreographer, and performer based in Grand Rapids, MI. She was introduced to Lindy Hop and vernacular jazz over a decade ago and hasn't stopped groovin' since. She was invited to join the Lindy Focus Residency Program in 2025 and holds competitive titles at events such as Second City Swingout, Dayton Swing Smackdown, and more. SB is a co-founder of Rapid Rhythms Swing Dance Community, where she teaches weekly classes and coaches performance and competitive teams. 

SB firmly believes dancing is for everybody and every body. Her classes are known for being lively, interactive, and adaptive to her students.


Pricing:
Pay-What-You-Can $10-30 per week
*If cost is a barrier to you, please reach out to organizer@example.edu to discuss scholarship opportunities. We want everyone to be able to dance!
Paypal organizer@example.edu or bring cash or check to class - please arrive early to pay!
 
Register here!  

From Sunday, October 11, 2026 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM EDT at Hoover St Studio.

item.title: Bujinkan Budo Training Session
item.description:
Bujinkan Budo Training Session

"Ninpo is the essence of goshinjutsu (self-protection)."

 

During the Fall 2026 semester, Bujinkan Budo Club training will be held on Thursdays from 19:00 - 21:00 (7-9pm) at the Intramural Sports Building (IMSB) in Room MPR B. If you are interested in trying out a class, please send a message through Maize Pages or an email to organizer@example.edu. Beginners welcome; we train with people across all levels of experience!

 

- Learn self defense and physical coordination through Bujinkan taijiutsu (unarmed combat);
- Training at the Michigan Bujinkan Dojo is supportive and non-competitive, emphasizing relaxed but spirited and disciplined practice;
- Receive mentoring through the senpai/kohai (senior/junior) relationships fostered in the dojo.

 

What to bring: comfortable workout clothes, socks, and a water bottle!

-----

For more information, email us at organizer@example.edu or checkout our website (www.michiganbujinkan.com), which also includes a training schedule!

From Thursday, October 15, 2026 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM EDT at Intramural Sports Building Multi-Purpose Room B.
